observed_repository_evidence.finding: The existing create-only path research/tool_intelligence/claims/<research_id>/<claim_target>.json prevents exact-path duplication but does not prevent semantically equivalent objectives when concurrent workers independently invent different research_id values.

During the active F2-WP-803 held-out world-model benchmark window, multiple Trigger-6 commits independently claimed overlapping E1 objectives under differently named research IDs (heldout prediction, selective prediction, proper scoring/abstention, prediction benchmark). At least one overlapping E1 source audit was completed at commit ffa2b0473b1e93986e8412db6133a106115cf120 while this worker's separately named E1 claim already existed. These receipts are complementary/duplicate-family evidence, not independent replication.

The claims README correctly says one create-only file per research objective, but the mutex namespace is keyed beneath worker-selected research_id. Therefore the protocol states semantic uniqueness without providing a deterministic cross-worker key that enforces it.

external_primary_inputs.use: Deterministic canonical serialization can make a structured objective descriptor hash-stable across workers.
Name-based identifiers demonstrate deterministic identity derived from a namespace plus name; this is an identity-design analogue, not a requirement to use UUIDv5.

A caller-independent operation key is the relevant idempotency pattern: retries/duplicates should converge on one logical operation identity rather than minting new operations from transport attempts. The document is an Internet-Draft, not a final RFC.

external_primary_inputs.source: Git content-addressed object identity / SHA-256 transition documentation
external_primary_inputs.use: Content-derived identifiers are an engineering analogue for deriving coordination identity from canonical descriptor content rather than human naming.

architecture_delta.problem: research_id is provenance identity, not a safe semantic mutex identity

objective_descriptor.target_refs: sorted exact canonical target refs, including workpackage/generation where material
objective_descriptor.subject_refs: sorted exact external/internal subject identifiers or claim IDs
objective_descriptor.discriminator_kind: controlled enum plus deterministic parameters; never free-form model prose
objective_descriptor.review_basis: null for original objective; exact superseding architecture-delta/evidence ref for legitimate stale re-review

proposal.canonicalization: RFC8785/JCS or an equivalently specified deterministic canonical serializer
proposal.research_id_role: human/provenance label referenced by the objective claim; it MUST NOT mint a second mutex identity
proposal.snapshot_role: moving F2 main SHA is bound as observation metadata but excluded from the base objective key unless an explicit review_basis declares a materially changed architecture; otherwise rapid main movement would defeat deduplication

fail_closed_rules: If two workers cannot independently normalize the descriptor to the same bytes, no material evidence work starts until the descriptor contract is resolved.
Free-form hypotheses, worker IDs, timestamps and arbitrary research_id strings MUST NOT participate in semantic mutex identity.
Fuzzy/LLM semantic similarity may warn about possible duplicates but MUST NOT grant, deny or replace the deterministic claim authority.
A legitimate stale re-review receives a new objective key only through an exact review_basis/superseding-delta reference.
Existing claim/receipt history remains append-only; duplicate historical claims are reconciled rather than deleted or rewritten.
architecture_delta.expected_benefit: Reduces parallel research token/tool waste and false independent-replication impressions while preserving provenance and one canonical coordination surface.
architecture_delta.runtime_efficiency: Coordination hashing is deterministic and negligible relative to duplicated external research; no model call is required for mutex admission.

counterhypotheses: A structured descriptor may under-deduplicate if equivalent objectives use different target decompositions.
An overly coarse descriptor may over-deduplicate legitimately distinct falsifiers.
A global objective index may add coordination contention under very high write concurrency.
The simplest sufficient repair may be a narrower workpackage+stage+objective-kind key instead of a general descriptor hash.
falsifiers_and_acceptance_gates: Concurrency fixture: N workers independently describe the same objective with different research_id/worker/timestamp values and all derive exactly one objective_key; exactly one create-only claim succeeds.
Distinct-falsifier fixture: two materially different discriminators on the same workpackage/stage derive different keys.
Moving-head fixture: harmless main-head movement alone does not create a new key.
Stale-review fixture: exact superseding architecture delta in review_basis intentionally creates a new key while preserving linkage to the original objective.
Canonicalization fixture: reordered JSON keys and target-ref ordering canonicalize identically.
No fuzzy model output participates in the authoritative mutex decision.

handoff.recommended_scope: Implement the smallest deterministic objective-key helper + create-only objective_claims surface + regression tests, then update Trigger-6 protocol to make research_id provenance-only.
handoff.reason: The defect is actively consuming duplicate research effort and can mislabel correlated duplicate work as separate evidence.
